entry.title: F-22 Pilot Controls FQ-44 Fighter Drone From The Cockpit For The First Time
entry.summary: A pilot flying an F-22 Raptor fighter has issued commands to a YFQ-44A Fury Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) drone in a first-of-its-kind test. An Anduril spokesperson confirmed directly to TWZ that this was a first for an F-22 and a pre-production YFQ-44A. “During the demonstration, an F-22 pilot served as an airborne ‘quarterback,’ issuing high-level tactical directives to a single YFQ-44A,” according to a press release from the Air Force . “The aircraft’s onboard autonomy software interpreted and executed those directives in real time, conducting dynamic flight maneuvers and simulated combat tasks.” A stock picture of an F-22 Raptor test jet. USAF “The event brought together personnel from the 412th Test Wing, 422nd Test and Evaluation Squadron, 309th Software Engineering Group, Experimental Operations Unit, F-22 System Program Office and the CCA Software Autonomy and Teaming Branch,” according to the Air Force release. The Experimental Operations Unit (EOU) mentioned here is based at Nellis Air Force Base in Nevada and has been leading efforts to pave the way for future Air Force CCA operations. The “Fury and an F-22 both took off [from] Edwards AFB [Air Force Base in California] and joined up midair,” according to a separate release from Anduril. “While in flight, the Raptor pilot sent an updated mission plan to Fury using a tactical data link, commanding Fury through operationally-relevant maneuvers from the cockpit of the crewed quarterback.” Neither the Air Force nor Anduril provided further details on how the F-22 was configured for this test. 关键事实：An Anduril spokesperson confirmed directly to TWZ that this was a first for an F-22；a pre-production YFQ-44A

entry.title: Order to limit Starshield for Ukraine came from inside White House, sources say
entry.summary: The order to limit a satellite system used by Ukraine for battlefield communications and drone operations came from inside the White House, according to two U.S. officials and a Western official briefed on the matter. The officials said leaders at the Defense Department received a message that the SpaceX Starshield service for the Ukrainian military needed to be slowed. The officials, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, did not specify who in the White House made the decision or who was responsible for implementing the order. The Pentagon is the biggest customer of Starshield, which is the military-grade version of the Starlink service. Ukrainian officials said this week that military-grade Starlink receptors stopped working in Ukraine when mounted on fast-moving objects, interfering with the performance of ‌Ukrainian drones that rely on them for onboard guidance systems over Ukrainian territory. U.S. pressures Ukraine over refinery attacks The move to temporarily restrict the vital communications system came as President Donald Trump has pressured Kyiv to stop its attacks on Russian refineries, which he has blamed for the soaring energy prices that are denting his Republican Party’s prospects in the November midterm elections. In response to a request for comment about the order to limit Starshield, a senior U.S. official said: “No such request was ever made by the president.” The White House did not respond to questions about whether other administration officials might have made the request. 关键事实：The order to limit a satellite system used by Ukraine for battlefield communications；drone operations came from inside the White House；according to two U.S

entry.title: What is Starshield, SpaceX’s military version of Starlink?
entry.summary: Ukraine said on Wednesday that Elon Musk’s SpaceX had restricted “military-grade” Starlink services, hampering Ukrainian drone strike missions and air defenses. The complaint has drawn renewed attention to the distinction between Starlink, SpaceX’s commercial satellite internet service, and Starshield , a military version developed for the Pentagon. “Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the U.S. government,” Musk said on Wednesday in a post on X, adding that any limits on speed or usage are decided by the U.S. military or the president. “Starlink is a commercial service owned and controlled by SpaceX. Usage of Starlink is limited to civilian or defensive activities and cannot be used for offensive military action, as doing so would be inappropriate for a commercial company.” WHAT IS STARLINK? Starlink, the main profit engine of SpaceX, is a satellite internet network of more than 11,000 satellites that beam broadband service directly to user terminals about the size of a folded newspaper. Since launching its first Starlink satellites in 2019 aboard reusable SpaceX rockets, the company has built a vast low-Earth-orbit constellation that blankets much of the planet, delivering faster connections than traditional communications satellites, which typically operate much farther from Earth and in far smaller numbers. But Musk has restricted Starlink for certain military uses while highlighting Starshield, a more secure network developed for government and military missions. 关键事实：Ukraine said on Wednesday that Elon Musk’s SpaceX had restricted “military-grade” Starlink services；hampering Ukrainian drone strike missions；air defenses

entry.title: What The Army’s Pacific Commanders Are Learning From Ukraine And Iran Conflicts
entry.summary: Army leaders preparing for a potential fight in the Pacific told us that some of the biggest lessons they’ve learned from the war in Ukraine and America’s now-paused fight against Iran are to move around assets that you can and find a better way to camouflage those that you can’t. The ubiquity of drones in Ukraine providing constant overwatch and strike capabilities, and U.S. troops killed and equipment destroyed or damaged by massive Iranian barrages on static installations are informing changes to how the Army trains, equips and operates. “A lot of the things that are happening right now in terms of long-range fires, integrated air and missile defense , and the lessons that we’re learning from them, we’re able to bring a lot of that to our potential challenges in the Pacific,” Gen. Ron Clark, commander of U.S. Army Pacific (USARPAC), told us at a media roundtable. So it’s one of those age-old Army forgotten sciences of how to hide in plain sight and how to camouflage ourselves from observation , because the ability to be able to see surface entities is almost ubiquitous.” “Our ability to be able to use electronic warfare , to be able to use just good old-fashioned camouflage, and the ability to deceive our adversary is a must,” Clark added. 关键事实：Army leaders preparing for a potential fight in the Pacific told us that some of the biggest lessons they’ve learned from the war in Ukraine

entry.title: Naval Group rolls out 5th Suffren-class attack submarine
entry.summary: Naval Group has rolled out Rubis (S639), the fifth Barracuda type nuclear attack submarine (SSN), transferring the vessel to its shiplift in Cherbourg ahead of sea trials for the French Navy. Naval Group press release On 16 October 2026, the fifth submarine of the Barracuda programme has left its construction hall in order to be transferred to the DME floating platform-type shiplift, in the presence of Catherine Vautrin, French minister for the Armed Forces and Veterans. 关键事实：Naval Group has rolled out Rubis (S639)；the fifth Barracuda type nuclear attack submarine (SSN)；transferring the vessel to its shiplift in Cherbourg ahead of sea trials for the French Navy

entry.title: Blue Origin to add new Florida launch pads, seeks aggressive increase in New Glenn flight rate
entry.summary: Graphic: Blue Origin Blue Origin said it will add new launch pads on Florida’s Space Coast to help ramp up the flight rate of its New Glenn rockets, as the company recovers from a catastrophic test fire explosion in May. In a series of other infrastructure announcements Friday morning, Ian Richardson, the Senior Vice President of Operations at Blue Origin, said the company was serious about launching and landing more rockets. “As we look ahead, this infrastructure is designed to support multiple flights per week by the end of the decade.” The new pads would be modeled after Blue Origin facilities at Launch Complex 36 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station. LC-36A, which is being rebuilt after the static test fire explosion, serves the New Glenn 7×2 rocket and LC-36B is under construction to support launches of the 9×4 variant of the rocket, which features nine BE-4 engines on the first stage and four BE-3U engines on the upper stage. Spectators along the beach in Cape Canaveral, Florida, enjoy a spectacular Sunday morning launch, taking in the view of a Blue Origin New Glenn rocket blasting off carrying a next-generation cellular broadband satellite. The company said later the AST SpaceMobile Bluebird 7 satellite ended up in the wrong orbit. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is in the middle of a 30-day comment period as it seeks public input on Blue Origin’s request to increase its launch cadence at LC-36A from 12 permitted flights up to 50. A virtual public hearing is scheduled for Thursday, Oct. 22, and public comment closes on Oct. 30. 关键事实：In a series of other infrastructure announcements Friday morning

entry.title: NASA Names Stephen Cash Marshall Space Flight Center Director
entry.summary: Photo of Stephen Cash NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman has named Stephen Cash director of the agency’s Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, effective Monday, Oct. 19. Cash, a veteran NASA engineer and aerospace executive, returns to lead the center where he began his career more than four decades ago. “Marshall contributions to NASA’s missions are historic and it’s no question why it’s the Center of Excellence for propulsion,” said Isaacman. 关键事实：effective Monday；a veteran NASA engineer

entry.title: Google's Gemini 4 Argon is closer to the AI frontier than any Google model in months
entry.summary: Google Deepmind's new frontier model, Gemini 4 Argon, scored 97.5 percent on ARC-AGI-3 at a cost of $4,800 using the "Provider Adapter Harness," a test setup that uses vendor-specific features like retained reasoning and context compaction. According to ARC Prize, Google is now the second AI lab after OpenAI to cross the 95 percent mark on what is widely considered the toughest benchmark for general problem-solving. Only GPT-6 Astra scores higher at 99.9 percent. Like Astra, Argon needed 62 percent fewer actions than the human baseline across the 25 public games. 关键事实：Google Deepmind's new frontier model；Gemini 4 Argon

entry.title: Germany Publishes National Post-Quantum Cryptography Migration Guideline
entry.summary: Insider Brief Germany’s BMI, BMDS and BSI have published a national guideline for implementing the EU roadmap for transitioning to post-quantum cryptography (PQC). The guideline recommends completing migrations for high-risk systems by the end of 2030 at the latest and largely completing the broader transition by 2035. The recommendations call for clear migration responsibilities and deadlines, systematic quantum-risk assessments, early coordination with manufacturers and supply chains, and cryptographic agility. PRESS RELEASE — Quantum computers pose an increasingly real threat to the security of cryptographic methods and thus to cybersecurity itself. The Federal Ministry of the Interior (BMI), the Federal Ministry for Digital Affairs and State Modernization (BMDS) and the Federal Office for Information Security (BSI) are now jointly publishing the Guideline for the implementation of the EU Roadmap on Post-Quantum Cryptography for Germany. It stems from an initiative by EU member states that had put forward recommendations for an EU-wide coordinated transition to quantum-safe cryptography, so-called post-quantum cryptography (PQC). Objectives of the Guideline The national guideline is aimed particularly at federal, state and local governments, as well as organizations and companies, including operators of critical infrastructure. 关键事实：Insider Brief Germany’s BMI；BSI have published a national guideline for implementing the EU roadmap for transitioning to post-quantum cryptography (PQC)；The guideline recommends completing migrations for high-risk systems by the end of 2030 at the latest
